title: Sentry ledger — overnight handoff (draft)
content:
Quick context:
This is a lightweight handoff ledger for the overnight Sentry window. Not a canonical runbook yet — cobbled notes + temporary mitigations. Use only if pager fires and you need a fast path to triage.

Current system state (as of last check, 23:40 PT):
- Hosted API: healthy, P95 latency ~ 170ms across us-west-2. Small read spike at 22:50 but auto-burst handled it.
- Dedicated pool (prod-dedicated-1): 82% GPU util, no OOMs.
- Cache layer (redis-inline): 5 keys evicted/minute, TTL churn from recent rollout (INF-3245) — expected.
- Active pagers: none. Scheduled grok job (seq-agg) will run at 01:10, may create transient load.

Known flakies / things to watch:
- model-warmup job sometimes leaves orphaned processes (seen 2x last week). If CPU jumps on serving nodes, check 'ps aux | grep warmup' and kill orphaned pids. Ticket: INF-3178.
- ephemeral 503s on /v1/generate when request size > 4k tokens and fallback routing hits older model variant. Quick fix: route-through small-burst (see routing-cmd below).

Pager-first-triage checklist (TL;DR):
1) Read pager message. Identify alert name and affected region.
2) Hit dashboard: Console -> Per-route -> /v1/generate -> last 15m. Check token-rate, error-rate, latency.
3) Run health checks:
   - curl -sS https://infra-health.internal/health || echo "health fail"
   - kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=redwood-serving -o wide
4) If 5xx spike: check logs for model fallback: kubectl logs <pod> -c serving | grep FALLBACK
5) If GPU OOM: check node metrics and restart pod with kc restart (see emergency commands).

Emergency commands (use carefully):
- Drain node: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Restart serving deployment (graceful): kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-serving -n prod
- Force route small-burst to hosted: infractl route set --route /v1/generate --policy burst-hosted --duration 10m
- Clear prefix cache for a model: redis-cli -h redis-cache-01 KEYS "cache:model:<model-name>:*" | xargs -r redis-cli -h redis-cache-01 DEL

Temporary mitigation recipes (if observed issues):
- Symptom: sustained P95 > 700ms, tokens/sec roughly constant.
  Mitigation: enable reduced-batching for that model for 5m: infractl config set --model <model-name> --batching reduced --ttl 5m and monitor. If latency drops, plan longer config change during day.

- Symptom: 503 flood tied to fallback routing.
  Mitigation: revert routing policy to previous stable commit: git checkout <sha> && infractl apply routes --file routes/stable.json. If repo commit unknown, route to hosted as hotfix.

Escalation matrix (who to ping):
- First: oncall-sre (pager) -> check channel #infra-alerts.
- Second: Marco Reyes (serving-runtime) -> slack @marco (oncall rotation).
- Third: Elliot Zhang (platform eng) -> call if decision required for capacity scaling.
- If legal/PSI: ping oncall-security -> follow security checklist in Confluence.

Open TODOs for next-day cleanup (assignments):
- INF-3245: revert temporary TTL changes after morning deploy (assigned: Nina).
- INF-3178: add watchdog for warmup process and auto-kill after 10m (assigned: Marco).
- Add bake-in test: simulate seq-agg job load and verify autoscaling (assigned: Elliot).

Notes to self / gotchas:
- When forcing route to hosted, watch cost (token spike) — set alert to kill route after 10m.
- Some infractl commands require elevated role; use `sudo infractl auth assume --role ops-override` and revert immediately.
- If doing redis mass deletes, start with a subset: redis-cli --scan --pattern "cache:model:<model-name>:prefix:*" | head -n 100 | xargs -r redis-cli -h redis-cache-01 DEL

Mini-runbook draft (to be formalized):
- Step 0: Confirm alert (as above), identify scope (route, model, region).
- Step 1: Reduce blast radius: set fallback-policy to single-variant, disable canary for route.
- Step 2: Apply temporary batching override (reduced) for model.
- Step 3: If still failing, route-of-last-resort -> hosted for 10m and file incident.
- Step 4: Collect logs: pod logs, gateway logs, model-vm logs, and mark relevant time window. Attach log snippets to incident JIRA.
- Step 5: Reconcile and plan durable fix during daytime.

Unresolved questions (for morning):
- Why did cache TTL roll increase post deploy? Is there a missing migration?
- Are warmup or prefetch jobs being reaped properly after model swap?

Scratch checklist before logging off:
- Confirm no active pagers in last 30m.
- Post to #infra-handovers: short summary + any ongoing mitigations.
- Set personal reminder to check INF-3245 at 09:15 PT.

References / shortcuts: (keep these handy)
- Dashboards: https://console.redwood-internal/dashboards/route/v1-generate
- Runbook index: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/serving-runtime
- Infractl docs: https://gitlab.redwood/infra/infractl/README.md

End of ledger. Keep this minimal and ephemeral — convert to formal runbook when time allows.

Rapid notes (random):
- If warmup pids stuck, command to list with start times: ps -eo pid,etime,cmd | grep warmup
- When restarting deployment, watch rollout status: kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-serving -n prod --watch
- If escalation needed after 30m unresolved, start postmortem stub (INF-xxxx) and flag SEV classification.

-- Nina
